claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in the starting simple-solid-solution state has relatively low hardness and strength.
The low hardness and strength are governed by the absence of effective microstructural obstacles to dislocation motion.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi alloy is a single-phase, relatively coarse-grained solid solution without secondary phases or strengthening precipitates.
Deformation in the starting state is dominated by facile grain-boundary-mediated plasticity.
Dislocation flow in the starting state is relatively unimpeded.
Facile grain-boundary plasticity and unimpeded dislocation flow explain the combination of favorable plasticity and machinability with low deformation resistance.
The homogeneous CoCrFeNiTi solid solution lacks significant lattice barriers, including strong lattice-distortion barriers and precipitate pinning.
Thermo-mechanical processing can significantly refine the grain structure while retaining the overall equimolar CoCrFeNiTi composition.
Thermo-mechanical processing can produce controlled fine precipitates in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Additional grain boundaries created by refinement act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Fine precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
Grain refinement or precipitate formation will increase the alloy's hardness and yield strength relative to the coarse-grained baseline.
The processed material will exhibit higher nanoindentation hardness than the baseline.
Processing will shift deformation from grain-boundary sliding toward dislocation pile-up or otherwise impeded dislocation motion.
The proposed mechanism applies at room temperature under quasi-static loading.
The mechanism may not apply at high strain rates, at extreme temperatures, or when secondary phases are already present.
A processed and an untreated equimolar CoCrFeNiTi sample set should be compared using nanoindentation and uniaxial tension or compression at ambient temperature.
Failure to obtain at least a 20% increase in both hardness and yield strength, or failure to observe the proposed mechanism shift, is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Grain boundaries are presented both as obstacles that impede dislocations and as the pathway for dominant facile grain-boundary sliding, without specifying the grain-size or deformation-regime transition that reconciles these roles.

The proposed intervention may deliberately introduce secondary precipitates, while the stated applicability boundary says the hypothesis may not apply when secondary phases are present; it is not clarified whether that exclusion applies only to the baseline.
